independent_czechoslovak_state_day.intro: On 28 October, Czechia commemorates the establishment of independent Czechoslovakia in 1918. It is a central national holiday connecting the present with the birth of the republic.
independent_czechoslovak_state_day.history: As Austria-Hungary collapsed at the end of the First World War, the Czechoslovak National Committee proclaimed an independent state in Prague on 28 October 1918. Tomáš Garrigue Masaryk became its first president. Czechia retains the anniversary after the peaceful division of Czechoslovakia in 1993.
independent_czechoslovak_state_day.traditions: Flags, wreath-laying ceremonies and cultural programmes mark the day. The President traditionally presents state decorations at Prague Castle. Museums and historic institutions may offer special visits or open days.
funFacts: The anniversary commemorates the state founded in 1918, not the formation of Czechia in 1993.
Masaryk’s initials T. G. are widely used in memorials and place names.
The Order of the White Lion is the country’s highest state decoration.
